headline: Metals and Gas Rally Hard as Precious Outflows Pause and Supply Fears Mount
paragraphs: Natural gas surged 10.31 percent to $3.61 per MMBtu, with rallies hinging on forecasts of prolonged cold weather. Silver leaped 9.35 percent to $43.80 per oz, leading a broader precious metals recovery as the gold-silver ratio fell, helping silver stage a hammer-pattern rebound despite its wider downtrend. Palladium jumped 8.71 percent to $903.50 per oz following a drop to its lowest level since 2017, while platinum gained 6.78 percent to $1325.60 per oz. Copper rose 5.85 percent to $5.64 per lb as prices rebounded following a steep monthly decline and technical bear-market repair. Gold climbed 3.55 percent to $3661.30 per oz, rebounding from 15-month and one-year lows as artificial intelligence jitters eased and rate fears subsided. WTI crude increased 2.49 percent to $85.76 per bbl.

Conversely, Brent crude fell 2.51 percent to $92.24 per bbl. The cause behind WTI's rise is unclear from the headlines, though overall oil markets reacted to mine strikes on ships reviving supply concerns alongside Saudi strike reports, while OPEC+ considered sticking with current quotas. The euro traded at 1.0977 against the US dollar, with no notable exchange rate movement mentioned.
